flag: Architecture::iteregion (seam-copied in build_arch_handle); addlflag pcodeop_addlflags::kuna_iteregion (0x2000) marks the matched CBRANCH
runtime_choice_rationale: The diamond->ternary rewrite reproduces the source ONLY when the source used a `?:` ternary; an explicit if/else compiles to the SAME object code, which the binary cannot distinguish. So this ships default-OFF and is flipped PER FUNCTION by an agent (kuna catalog -> --option iteregion on): ON for format/print/flag-heavy code where the ternary form dominates (compilers turn `cond ? "%s," : "%s"` into exactly this assignment diamond), OFF where explicit if/else is the likely source.
when_to_flip_on: Flip iteregion ON for a function when kuna emits repeated two-arm assignment diamonds `if (c) v = A; else v = B;` whose arms are single COPYs to the same variable feeding a use (print/format/flag helpers: iproute2 print_link_flags, coreutils output_* helpers, any `flags ? "%s," : "%s"` idiom), and the source plausibly used `?:`. Leave OFF when the diamonds likely came from explicit if/else in the source (control-flow-heavy code), since ON would invent a ternary the author never wrote.
speed_note: Whole-binary load+analysis of `ip` dominates (~9s, identical on/off); the iteregion pass is a single linear post-structuring walk over the structured blocks of one function, so its own cost is in the noise (ON measured marginally faster than OFF).
root_cause: At -O0 a source ternary (`flags ? "%s," : "%s"`) compiles to a two-arm register-assignment diamond (`lea rax, "%s,"` / `lea rax, "%s"`). Ghidra/kuna's collapse-based structurer renders each diamond as a literal `if (c) { v = A } else { v = B }` statement pair, doubling the branch count. On print_link_flags kuna emitted 41 ifs / 0 ternaries (232 LOC) vs source/angr 21 ifs / 20 ternaries (107 LOC), GED 140.
mechanism: New S8 pass kuna-decomp/src/s8_structure/kuna_iteregion.rs (ActionIteRegion, scheduled after dedupitetail in universalaction.rs): after structuring, match a narrow two-arm assignment diamond -- a 3-component BlockIf with no own goto, a condition leaf whose LAST printed op is the CBRANCH (leading `flags &= ~IFF_x` statements allowed), and both clauses a single-COPY-to-the-same-variable leaf. It sets a print-only addlflag (kuna_iteregion, 0x2000) on the matched CBRANCH; NO p-code is cloned or mutated. The one genuinely new piece is the S9 emit hook: PrintC::emit_block_if, seeing a marked BlockIf, re-derives the match (match_ite_assignment, shared with the pass) and emits `dest = ( cond ) ? A : B;` -- the condition via the normal ONLY_BRANCH CBRANCH render (boolean-flip aware), each arm's RHS via op_push_ir on an empty RPN stack (the direct-resolution engine drains each sub-expression), leading condition statements emitted normally first. Ghidra's printc has no ternary operator, so the emit hook is contained to one method. Default-OFF: with the option off the pass never runs, no flag is set, and output is byte-identical.
notes: print_link_flags: 41 ifs/0 ternaries/232 LOC -> 22 ifs/20 ternaries/140 LOC; 19/20 diamonds rewritten (the `is_json_context() ? ...` head site is left if/else). GED 140 -> 11 (delta -129). Not GED 0: the remaining 11 is the un-folded single-use temp (kuna emits `v = c?A:B; sub(...,v,...)` where angr folds the ternary into the call argument -- a deliberate follow-up increment, NOT this PR) plus the raw string-pointer constants in the arms. make test PARITY OK (675/675, default-off byte-identical). make test-stages PARITY OK. make rust-test green.
